title: Conservation of Energy and Resources
seo_title: Grade 5 Science: Conservation of Energy and Resources Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Identify forms of energy and energy transformations; distinguish renewable and non-renewable energy sources; assess the effects of energy use on the environment and ways to conserve energy and resources. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand E: Earth and Space Systems – Conservation of Energy and Resources)
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 science worksheets on forms of energy, energy changes, renewable and non-renewable resources, Ontario electricity and saving energy. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Energy changes form; it is not used up.
key_sub: Renewable sources do not run out; conserving energy saves resources and reduces pollution.
body_html:
How to think about it

Energy cannot be made or destroyed, only changed from one form to another.

  • Forms of energy: kinetic, potential, thermal, light, sound, electrical, chemical.
  • Renewable sources: sun, wind, moving water, biomass. Non-renewable: coal, oil, natural gas, uranium.
  • Ontario's electricity comes mostly from nuclear and hydroelectric power.
  • Turning things off, using LED bulbs and Energy Star appliances, and reducing waste conserve energy.
Example

What energy change happens in a solar panel?

light in

electricity out

Answer: light → electrical

Example

Is natural gas renewable?

it took millions of years to form

Answer: no

Common mistakes

  • Thinking energy gets used up and disappears.
  • Thinking renewable sources have no drawbacks.
  • Mixing up energy sources and forms of energy.

faq.q: What is the difference between renewable and non-renewable energy?
faq.a: Renewable energy comes from sources that are replaced naturally, like wind. Non-renewable sources, like oil, run out.

faq.q: Where does Ontario's electricity come from?
faq.a: Mostly from nuclear power stations and hydroelectric dams, plus wind, solar and natural gas.
Turn off lights and devices, use LED bulbs, keep doors and windows closed when heating or cooling, and dress for the weather.

items.q: Why do we need energy?
c: to move, grow and keep our bodies working
items.e: Living things need energy for life processes.

items.q: Which form of energy does gasoline in a car's tank mainly have?
items.e: Energy is stored in the substances in it.

items.q: Where did the energy in the rice we eat first come from?
items.e: The rice plant used light energy from the Sun to make food.

items.q: Which form of energy does a pupil standing at the top of a slide mainly have?
items.e: It is raised above the ground.

items.q: Why is energy never really 'used up'?
c: It changes from one form to another.
items.e: Energy is conserved.

items.q: Can energy be created or destroyed?
c: No. It can only be converted from one form to another.
items.e: The total amount of energy stays the same.

items.q: What is energy?
c: the ability to do work or make things move or change
items.e: Energy makes things happen.

items.q: Where did the energy in a chicken drumstick first come from?
items.e: The chicken ate plants, which got their energy from the Sun.

items.q: Which form of energy is in a stretched rubber band?
items.e: Stretching stores energy.

items.q: What is the main source of energy for the Earth?
items.e: Plants, animals, food and fuels all depend on the Sun.

items.q: Which form of energy does the current in a wire to a lamp mainly have?
items.e: This is electrical energy.

items.q: Which form of energy does a piece of charcoal for a barbecue mainly have?
items.e: Energy is stored in the substances in it.

items.q: What energy change happens in a solar panel?
items.e: Solar cells change light into electricity.

items.q: What does 'reduce, reuse, recycle' help save?
c: resources and the energy needed to make new things
items.e: Making new products uses energy.

items.q: Where did the electricity from a solar panel first come from?
items.e: The solar panel converts light energy from the Sun.

items.q: Which is a renewable energy source?
items.e: Wind will not run out.

items.q: Which form of energy does a battery mainly have?
items.e: Energy is stored in the substances in it.

items.q: Where did the energy of the wind first come from?
items.e: The Sun heats the land and air unevenly, which causes wind.

items.q: Which is a non-renewable energy source?
items.e: Fossil fuels took millions of years to form.

items.q: Which form of energy does the bent bow of an archer, ready to shoot mainly have?
items.e: It is stretched, bent or compressed.

items.q: A candle burns. Which shows the main energy conversion?
c: chemical potential energy → light energy and heat energy
light energy and heat energy → chemical potential energy
items.e: A candle burns: chemical potential energy → light energy and heat energy.

items.q: A solar panel on an HDB rooftop produces electricity. Which shows the main energy conversion?
items.e: A solar panel on an HDB rooftop produces electricity: light energy → electrical energy.

items.q: What is a disadvantage of burning fossil fuels?
c: It releases carbon dioxide and pollutes the air.
items.e: Fossil fuels add greenhouse gases.

items.q: A pupil cycles up a slope and stops at the top. Which shows the main energy conversion?
c: chemical potential energy → kinetic energy → gravitational potential energy
gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy → chemical potential energy
chemical potential energy → light energy and heat energy
chemical potential energy → electrical energy → light energy
items.e: A pupil cycles up a slope and stops at the top: chemical potential energy → kinetic energy → gravitational potential energy.

items.q: Which device changes electric energy into sound?
c: a toy car with a motor
items.e: Look at what goes in (electric energy) and what comes out (sound).

items.q: An electric drill changes electric energy into which main form of energy?
c: electric energy only, with no change
items.e: The main job of an electric drill is to make motion.

items.q: Which device changes light into electric energy?
items.e: Look at what goes in (light) and what comes out (electric energy).

items.q: A hand-crank flashlight changes motion (energy of motion) into which main form of energy?
items.e: The main job of a hand-crank flashlight is to make light.

items.q: Why should you put on a sweater instead of turning up the heat?
c: It makes the house warmer for everyone.
items.e: Conserving energy reduces pollution.

items.q: What is a disadvantage of wind turbines?
c: They only work when the wind blows.
items.e: Every source has pros and cons.

items.q: An electric fan changes electric energy into which main form of energy?
c: electric energy only, with no change
items.e: The main job of an electric fan is to make motion.

items.q: Which device changes electric energy into motion?
c: a bike light powered by the wheel
items.e: Look at what goes in (electric energy) and what comes out (motion).

items.q: Where does most of Ontario's electricity come from?
items.e: Ontario closed its coal plants in 2014.

items.q: A pupil rubs her hands together and they feel warm. Which shows the main energy conversion?
c: chemical potential energy → kinetic energy → gravitational potential energy
items.e: A pupil rubs her hands together and they feel warm: kinetic energy → heat energy.

items.q: Which device changes motion into electric energy?
items.e: Look at what goes in (motion) and what comes out (electric energy).

items.q: A doorbell changes electric energy into which main form of energy?
c: electric energy only, with no change
items.e: The main job of a doorbell is to make sound.

items.q: A battery powers a flashlight. Which shows the main energy conversion?
c: chemical potential energy → electrical energy → light energy
light energy → electrical energy → chemical potential energy
items.e: A battery powers a flashlight: chemical potential energy → electrical energy → light energy.

items.q: Which device changes electric energy into motion?
items.e: Look at what goes in (electric energy) and what comes out (motion).

items.q: A bike light powered by the wheel changes motion (energy of motion) into which main form of energy?
items.e: The main job of a bike light powered by the wheel is to make light.

items.q: A blender changes electric energy into which main form of energy?
c: electric energy only, with no change
items.e: The main job of a blender is to make motion.

items.q: A stretched elastic band stores which form of energy?
items.e: It is released when let go.

items.q: Benjamin reads about a resource that formed from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago. Which resource is it?
items.e: That is how rock salt formed.

items.q: Maya asks how copper and gold ores formed. What is the best explanation?
c: from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago
from iron that settled out of ancient oceans in layers
from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries
from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years
items.e: Copper and gold ores formed from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries.

items.q: What energy change happens when you rub your hands together?
items.e: Friction makes heat.

items.q: Which energy source is renewable?
items.e: Heat from inside Earth (geothermal) is renewed by nature and does not run out. Coal, oil and gas take millions of years to form.

items.q: Which energy source is renewable?
items.e: Flowing water is renewed by nature and does not run out. Coal, oil and gas take millions of years to form.

items.q: Jayden asks how coal formed. What is the best explanation?
c: from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years
from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years
from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago
from rain and snowmelt soaking into porous rock and sediment (aquifers)
items.e: Coal formed from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years.

items.q: Which action saves energy at home?
c: opening windows with the heat on
turning off lights when you leave a room
leaving the TV on all night
items.e: Small actions add up.

items.q: Which energy source is not renewable?
items.e: Oil formed over millions of years and will run out; burning it also pollutes the air.

items.q: Which is used to turn wind into electricity or motion?
c: a gas stove or gas power plant
a dam with a power plant
items.e: Energy from wind is used with wind turbines.

items.q: Emma asks how groundwater formed. What is the best explanation?
c: from rain and snowmelt soaking into porous rock and sediment (aquifers)
from iron that settled out of ancient oceans in layers
from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago
from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years
items.e: Groundwater formed from rain and snowmelt soaking into porous rock and sediment (aquifers).

items.q: People use a dam with a power plant to get energy from moving water. Which is a problem with this energy source?
c: Turbines can harm birds and bats, and they need steady wind.
Burning coal pollutes the air, and mining it damages land.
Burning gas pollutes the air, and drilling can harm land and water.
A dam floods land and blocks fish from swimming up the river.
items.e: A dam floods land and blocks fish from swimming up the river.

items.q: Which form of energy is stored in food?
items.e: Your body changes it into motion and heat.

items.q: People use gasoline in cars to get energy from oil. Which is a benefit of this energy source?
c: It is replaced naturally in a few days.
It stores a lot of energy in a small amount.
items.e: It stores a lot of energy in a small amount.

items.q: Which energy source is not renewable?
items.e: Natural gas formed over millions of years and will run out; burning it also pollutes the air.

items.q: Which is used to turn moving water into electricity or motion?
c: a gas stove or gas power plant
a dam with a power plant
items.e: Energy from moving water is used with a dam with a power plant.

items.q: Which is used to turn natural gas into electricity or motion?
c: a gas stove or gas power plant
items.e: Energy from natural gas is used with a gas stove or gas power plant.

items.q: Ava reads about a resource that formed from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries. Which resource is it?
items.e: That is how copper and gold ores formed.

items.q: People use solar panels to get energy from sunlight. Which is a problem with this energy source?
c: Panels need a lot of land or roof space, and they only work when the sun shines.
Burning gas pollutes the air, and drilling can harm land and water.
It only works in places with hot rock near the surface.
Burning coal pollutes the air, and mining it damages land.
items.e: Panels need a lot of land or roof space, and they only work when the sun shines.

items.q: Which energy source is not renewable?
items.e: Coal formed over millions of years and will run out; burning it also pollutes the air.

items.q: Which of the three R's is turning an old jar into a pencil holder?
items.e: Reusing means using something again for the same or a new job.

items.q: Which of the three R's is using the back of old paper for drawing?
items.e: Reusing means using something again for the same or a new job.

items.q: Which of the three R's is using a refillable water bottle?
items.e: Reusing means using something again for the same or a new job.

items.q: Plastic bags are blowing into the ocean and hurting sea turtles. Which solution best addresses this problem?
c: Use reusable cloth bags and ban single-use plastic bags.
Replant trees and protect part of the forest as a park.
Build wind turbines and solar panels.
Fix leaks and water lawns less often.
items.e: This solution deals with the cause of the problem. Use reusable cloth bags and ban single-use plastic bags.

items.q: Which of the three R's is printing on both sides of the paper?
items.e: Reducing means using less in the first place.

items.q: A forest is cut down and animals lose their homes. Which solution best addresses this problem?
c: Replant trees and protect part of the forest as a park.
Build a wildlife bridge over the highway.
Add bus lines and bike lanes so fewer people drive.
Start a recycling and composting program.
items.e: This solution deals with the cause of the problem. Replant trees and protect part of the forest as a park.

items.q: What does the Energy Star label on an appliance mean?
c: It runs on solar power only.
It uses less energy than similar models.
items.e: Look for efficient appliances.

items.q: How does a hydroelectric dam make electricity?
c: It uses sunlight on the water.
Falling water turns turbines connected to generators.
items.e: Niagara Falls has large hydro stations.

items.q: Which of the three R's is turning off lights in empty rooms?
items.e: Reducing means using less in the first place.

items.q: An old bulb uses 60 watts and an LED bulb that gives the same light uses 9 watts. A school replaces 8 old bulbs with LEDs. How many fewer watts are used when they are all on?
items.e: (60 − 9) × 8 = 408 watts. Using less electricity means less fuel burned at power plants.

items.q: Which of the three R's is packing lunch in a reusable box?
items.e: Reusing means using something again for the same or a new job.

items.q: Why are LED bulbs better than old incandescent bulbs?
c: They are brighter only because they are hot.
They give the same light using much less electricity.
items.e: Less energy is wasted as heat.

items.q: A town burns coal to make electricity, polluting the air. Which solution best addresses this problem?
c: Build wind turbines and solar panels.
Add garbage and recycling bins and hold clean-up days.
Use reusable cloth bags and ban single-use plastic bags.
Build a treatment plant that cleans wastewater before it is released.
items.e: This solution deals with the cause of the problem. Build wind turbines and solar panels.

items.q: An old bulb uses 60 watts and an LED bulb that gives the same light uses 9 watts. A school replaces 10 old bulbs with LEDs. How many fewer watts are used when they are all on?
items.e: (60 − 9) × 10 = 510 watts. Using less electricity means less fuel burned at power plants.

items.q: Soil washes off a farm field into a river after heavy rain. Which solution best addresses this problem?
c: Use reusable cloth bags and ban single-use plastic bags.
Plant cover crops and rows of trees to hold the soil.
Build wind turbines and solar panels.
Replant trees and protect part of the forest as a park.
items.e: This solution deals with the cause of the problem. Plant cover crops and rows of trees to hold the soil.

items.q: Factories release smoke with harmful gases. Which solution best addresses this problem?
c: Build a treatment plant that cleans wastewater before it is released.
Leave strips of plants along the water and use less fertilizer.
Add garbage and recycling bins and hold clean-up days.
items.e: This solution deals with the cause of the problem. Put filters (scrubbers) on smokestacks.

items.q: Fertilizer runoff makes algae grow over a pond. Which solution best addresses this problem?
c: Leave strips of plants along the water and use less fertilizer.
Add bus lines and bike lanes so fewer people drive.
Plant cover crops and rows of trees to hold the soil.
items.e: This solution deals with the cause of the problem. Leave strips of plants along the water and use less fertilizer.

items.q: Which of the three R's is taking glass bottles to be made into new glass?
items.e: Recycling means breaking a material down to make new products.

items.q: An old bulb uses 40 watts and an LED bulb that gives the same light uses 6 watts. A school replaces 8 old bulbs with LEDs. How many fewer watts are used when they are all on?
items.e: (40 − 6) × 8 = 272 watts. Using less electricity means less fuel burned at power plants.

items.q: An old bulb uses 40 watts and an LED bulb that gives the same light uses 6 watts. A school replaces 6 old bulbs with LEDs. How many fewer watts are used when they are all on?
items.e: (40 − 6) × 6 = 204 watts. Using less electricity means less fuel burned at power plants.

items.q: What percent of Oak Ridge's electricity comes from renewable sources?
items.e: Wind and solar (15%) + water (20%) = 35%.

items.q: Why do some cities build wetlands next to farms?
c: Wetland plants trap soil and fertilizer before they reach rivers.
items.e: Wetlands act like natural filters.

items.q: Students test whether plant roots stop erosion. They pour water on a tray of bare soil and a tray of soil with grass. Which result supports the idea?
c: Both trays lose the same amount.
Less soil washes off the tray with grass.
More soil washes off the grass tray.
items.e: Roots hold soil, so less is carried away.

items.q: Why is the inside of a solar oven often painted black?
c: Black takes in light and changes it into heat.
items.e: Dark colours absorb more light energy.

items.q: A town wants to know if its new recycling program works. What should it measure?
c: how many people like the program
the amount of garbage sent to the landfill before and after
items.e: Data before and after the change show whether less waste goes to the landfill.

items.q: A design must cost less than $10 and use only paper and tape. These limits are called
items.e: Constraints are limits on a design.

A shower uses about 8 litres of water per minute. Mei cuts her shower from 10 minutes to 6 minutes. How much water does that save in 7 days?
This graph shows where Riverton gets its electricity. Which source does Riverton use the most?
items.e: Wind and solar is the largest part of the circle.

items.q: A school installs solar panels. Which problem does this help with?
c: It reduces the electricity made by burning fossil fuels.
items.e: Solar panels make electricity without burning fuel.

items.q: What percent of Oak Ridge's electricity comes from fossil fuels?
items.e: Coal (10%) + natural gas (15%) = 25%.

items.e: Coal (5%) + natural gas (15%) = 20%.

items.q: Why is foil used inside a solar oven?
c: It reflects light onto the food.
items.e: More light reaching the food means more heat.
